findings.summary: Dev-note reports an unmeasurable byte count for the triage oversize corpus, violating spec §4.2 (⛔ 不得编造失败现象/未实测结果) and §6 (dev-note must carry 你构造的超限语料实际字节数). The note's table states the triage corpus is 150 692 字节 (~147 KB) as a measured figure, but the helper that would build it, makeOversizeTriageCorpus, is declared at test/g7-prompt-file.test.ts:43 and is never invoked anywhere in the repo (grep for makeOversizeTriageCorpus yields only its own definition; only makeOversizeEvidence is called, at line 65). No executed test ever serializes that corpus, so no vitest run could have produced 150 692. Spec §4.2 records that this line has already had two dev-notes report structurally impossible results, each overturned by review.

The >128 KB oversize property is never asserted on the triage path, leaving T1's decisive guarantee one-sided despite spec §1's ⛔ 两条路径都要改 rationale that triage fails identically once 板面一大. T1 constructs and asserts an oversize corpus only for generate (serializedBytes > 131072 at line 72; the per-arg < 131072 loop at lines 92-94). The triage case in T2 (lines 134-154) uses a single-clue corpus and asserts only that '--prompt-file' is present and no '--' separator exists — it never checks any argument's byte length, so it would pass even under an argv scheme that still breaks at real scale. Consequently the dev-note's claim that both corpora deliver with 'argv 中无任何单个参数 ≥ 131 072 字节' is unsupported for triage.

Dead test helper: makeOversizeTriageCorpus is defined but never referenced, leaving the test file asserting less than it appears to. Either wire it into a triage-side oversize assertion (preferred, as it would resolve the T1/T2 gap above) or remove it so the test file's stated coverage matches what actually executes.
